# PART 1 – Credibility and tools {.darkslide background-color="rgba(0,0,0,0)"}

::: {.partlabel}
Part 1 – 90 minutes
:::

::: notes
Part one, then. We start further back than you might expect, with what science is for, why anyone thinks it is in trouble, and the red-card study, in which twenty-nine teams analysed one dataset and disagreed. Then what open research proposes as the remedy, and how well that holds up. Then the evidence – three very large studies, published together, that put numbers on how often social-science findings survive being repeated – and a first look at the one of those studies that I took part in. And we finish on the tools, because every part of this, the sharing, the checking and the repeating, is something that software either makes easy or makes impossible.
:::
